message.content:
The Battle of Waterloo (18 June 1815) was one of the bloodiest single engagements of the Napoleonic Wars.  Contemporary estimates put the losses at roughly:

| Side | Killed | Wounded | Missing/Prisoners | **Total Casualties** |
|------|--------|---------|-------------------|----------------------|
| **Allied (British, Dutch‑German, Prussian)** | ~8 000 | ~12 000 | ~5 000 | **≈ 25 000** |
| **French** | ~8 000 | ~12 000 | ~5 000 | **≈ 25 000** |

So, in total, the battle produced about **50 000 casualties** (killed, wounded, missing, or captured).  These figures are rounded; different historians cite slightly different numbers, but the consensus is that each side suffered roughly 25 000 casualties.
